<!-- pr-reviewer: 9e311f317c9d45376f94a578327da05d834908ce -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** Reviewed under the safety floor, because the change alters posted G-code.

### What looks good
- The G84 tap feed now uses `fn()`: three decimals in mm, four decimals in inch (`assets/posts/mach4.cps` line 842). The issue asks for this.
- `tapPitchHolds()` compares the pitch of the written words with the stream pitch. It uses the written F (`fn`) and the written S (`Math.round(sRpm)`, the same rounding as `ni()` for the `S` block). It refuses an error above 0.01 percent by name (`who()` plus "canned cycle G84 (tap)"). This matches the `haas.cps` guard of #3694.
- The guard runs after the "no feed rate" and `spindleStopped` checks. Thus `feed > 0` and `sRpm > 0` are true when it runs. A NaN error also refuses (`!(error <= 1e-4)`).
- `ff()` does not change. Other Mach4 feeds and all other posts do not change. The diff in `assets/posts/` is only `mach4.cps`.
- The new test file is in the lowest crate (`camcraft-post`), with a provenance line and a Gate map.
- The decision file uses no outside material. It cites no HSMWorks or Autodesk post text.

### Results (trial merge with main `9dfcc7a`, clean, built locally)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-post --test mach4_feed_decimals` | 4 passed |
| Red-first: the same suite with main's `mach4.cps` | 4 failed (`F34.6` vs `F34.56`, `F1.36` vs `F1.3606`, no refusal in the two refusal pins) |
| `camcraft-post` mach4 suites: `mach4_post` 6, `mach4_trunnion` 7, `script_mach4` 11, `coincident_arcs` 8, `same_angle_arcs` 4, `same_angle_stream` 4, `upright_after_tilt` 13, `wcs_flip_dialects` 9 | all passed |
| `camcraft-app --test conformance` (pins `golden/nc/mach4/tap_plate.nc` `F750` and `synth_mach4.nc` `F240`) | 7 passed, goldens unchanged |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Heavy lanes
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --dry-run` reaches one step: `app heavy: probe_no_coolant`. That target has no `#[ignore]` test, so the step runs zero tests. No heavy test applies to this diff.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. The PR is still a draft. It must be flagged ready before the merge (Pull Request Law).
2. The pinning stream has a `Plunge ... F` move, but no test asserts its F word. `ff()` does not change, so the risk is low. A later assert would pin "other feeds keep one mm decimal".

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
